name: Coastal Environmental Studies, BS
degree: Bachelor of Science in Coastal Environmental Studies

requirements.label: foundation
requirements.title: Required Foundation Courses for Major (35 credits)

rules.manualCheck: Listed on the page as a standalone alternative to the other calculus sequences.

requirements.sourceText: AMS 102 - Elements of Statistics OR AMS 110 - Probability and Statistics in the Life Sciences; BIO 201 - Fundamentals of Biology: Organisms to Ecosystems; BIO 204 - Fundamentals of Scientific Inquiry in the Biological Sciences I; CHE 131 - General Chemistry IB; CHE 133 - General Chemistry Laboratory I AND CHE 132 - General Chemistry II (see Note 4); ENS 119 - Physics for Environmental Studies OR PHY 119 - Physics for Environmental Studies (see Note 3); MAT 131 - Calculus I; MAT 132 - Calculus II OR MAT 125 - Calculus A OR MAT 130 - Trigonometry and Logarithms, MAT 125 - Calculus A, MAT 126 - Calculus B OR AMS 151 - Applied Calculus I, AMS 161 - Applied Calculus II; SUS 111 - Introduction to Sustainability OR ENS 101 - Prospects for Planet Earth; SUS 113 - Physical Geography Lecture OR GEO 102 - The Earth; SUS 201 - Systems and Models

requirements.label: foundation-math-placement
requirements.title: Math placement requirement

rule.manualCheck: Confirm whether the student placed into MAT 125, MAT 131, or AMS 151; if not, MAT 123 (or MAT 119 and MAT 123) is required.
rule.text: If students do not place into MAT 125 or MAT 131 or AMS 151 on the basis of the math placement examination, MAT 123 (or MAT 119 /MAT 123) is a required course for the major.
rule.reason: Conditional on math placement examination results, which are not a transcript course rule.

requirements.sourceText: SUS 301 - Technical Writing and Communication; SUS 305 - Collective Action and Advocacy OR ENS 301 - Contemporary Environmental Issues and Policies

requirements.label: core
requirements.title: Core Courses

rules.manualCheck: Page notes CHE 311 was formerly offered as ENV 321.

requirements.sourceText: ATM 305 - Global Atmospheric Change OR ENV 304 - Global Environmental Change; BIO 351 - Ecology; ENV 320 - Chemistry for Environmental Scientists; CHE 311 - Environmental Chemistry Lab (formerly offered as ENV 321); GSS 313 - GIS Design and Application I; GSS 314 - GIS Laboratory

requirements.label: group-a
requirements.title: Group A: Environmental Science Electives (choose 9 credits)
requirements.sourceText: Students are required to select 9 credits from group A and 6 credits from group B. Group A: Environmental Science Electives (choose 9 credits): BIO 352 - Ecology Laboratory *; CHE 312 - Physical Chemistry for the Life Sciences *; CHE 321 - Organic Chemistry I; ENS 311 - Ecosystem Ecology and the Global Environment; BIO 386 - Ecosystem Ecology and the Global Environment; ENV 310 - Sustainability and Renewable Energy - Costa Rica; ENV 315 - Principles and Applications of Groundwater Hydrology; GEO 315 - Groundwater Hydrology; ENV 316 - Coastal Zone Management; ENV 340 - Contemporary Topics in Environmental Science; GEO 313 - Understanding Water Resources for the 21st Century; GSS 354 - Geospatial Science for the Coastal Zone; MAR 303 - Long Island Marine Habitats; MAR 304 - Waves, Tides, and Beaches; MAR 308 - Environmental Instrumental Analysis *; MAR 315 - Marine Conservation; MAR 320 - Limnology; MAR 333 - Coastal Oceanography; MAR 336 - Marine Pollution; MAR 354 - Introduction to Geological Oceanography; MAR 388 - Tropical Marine Ecology; MAR 394 - Environmental Toxicology and Public Health; SUS 319 - Restoration Ecology

requirements.label: group-b
requirements.title: Group B: Environment, Society, and Policy (choose 6 credits)
requirements.sourceText: Group B: Environment, Society, and Policy (choose 6 credits): EDP 301 - Urban Systems *; EDP 305 - Risk Assessment and Sustainable Development; EDP 309 - Planning: Policies and Regulations *; ENV 339 - Economics of Coastal and Marine Ecosystems; SOC 344 - Environmental Sociology; SUS 311 - Disasters and Society: A Global Perspective *; SUS 317 - American Environmental History; SUS 318 - American Environmental Politics *; SUS 321 - Ecology and Evolution in American Literature; SUS 323 - Environmental Justice; SUS 324 - Human Geography and the Environment; SUS 325 - Environmental Writing and the Media; SUS 340 - Ecological and Social Dimensions of Disease; SUS 342 - Energy and Mineral Resources; SUS 366 - Philosophy of the Environment (III) *

requirements.label: systems
requirements.title: Systems Course (3 credits)
requirements.sourceText: One Integrative, Collaborative Systems Project course: ENS 443 - Environmental Problem Solving 3 credits; ENV 301 - Sustainability of the Long Island Pine Barrens 3 credits; ENV 487 - Research in Environmental Sciences 0-6 credits (see Note 1); ENV 488 - Internship in Coastal Environmental Studies 0-12 credits, (see Note 2); SUS 401 - Integrative, Collaborative Systems Studies 3 credits

requirements.label: upper-division-writing
requirements.title: Upper-Division Writing Requirement

rule.manualCheck: Requires registration in the 0-credit SUS 459 and approval of either a term paper or a laboratory report written for an advanced course in the appropriate major at Stony Brook (including Readings and Research courses). Completion of SUS 459 with a grade of S results in approval of the WRTD requirement. A list of preapproved courses can be obtained through the department.

requirements.sourceText: The advanced writing component of the major in COS requires registration in the 0-credit SUS 459 and approval of either a term paper or a laboratory report written for an advanced course in the appropriate major at Stony Brook (including Readings and Research courses). Completion of SUS 459 with a grade of S will result in approval of the WRTD requirement.

requirements.label: low-grade-exception
requirements.title: Limit on passing grades below C

rule.text: No more than one course (4 credits maximum) with a passing grade lower than C can be credited towards the major.
rule.reason: A program-wide cap on courses with grades below C that no rule type expresses.

requirements.sourceText: No more than one course (4 credits maximum) with a passing grade lower than C can be credited towards the major.

requirements.label: double-major-limit
requirements.title: Double major limit within SoMAS

rule.text: Excluding ENV 301, SUS 301, SUS 305, and SUS 401, no more than 6 credits of 300-400 level course credits can be applied to two majors within the School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences.
rule.reason: Cross-major credit limit that no rule type expresses.

requirements.sourceText: Excluding ENV 301 - Sustainability of the Long Island Pine Barrens , SUS 301 - Technical Writing and Communication , SUS 305 - Collective Action and Advocacy , and SUS 401 - Integrative, Collaborative Systems Studies , no more than 6 credits of 300-400 level course credits can be applied to two majors within the School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences.

policies.sourceText: Courses taken with the Pass/NC option may not be applied to the major.

notes.text: Program director: Katherine B. Aubrecht (katherine.aubrecht@stonybrook.edu). Undergraduate advisor: Nancy Black (nancy.black@stonybrook.edu). Program office: E2361 Melville Library, (631) 632-9404.
Completion of the major requires 73 credits. Courses taken with the Pass/NC option may not be applied to the major.
Courses marked with * have additional prerequisites outside of the major.
CHE 311 is formerly offered as ENV 321; the sample sequence lists ENV 320/ENV 321 together.

Study abroad experiences in Costa Rica, Madagascar, and the Turkana Basin (Kenya) are available; students should talk with the major director about how study abroad coursework can fulfill major requirements.
The Degree Requirements section also notes this degree prepares students for graduate study and entry-level employment; no admission requirements are listed for the major.
